cases.task: Create a visual identity from the direction: Bauhaus, vintage editorial, and a little surrealism.
expected_behavior: Do not generate a finished identity from generic reference labels
Request five to 10 specific human references and at least three anti-references
Explain what makes a reference system-generating

cases.task: Develop an identity for a new AI conference. The competitive field is dominated by black backgrounds, neon gradients, chrome, glowing orbs, and abstract 3D.
expected_behavior: Separate category-legibility codes from category wallpaper
Recommend which codes to retain, reject, invert, or replace
Identify visual white space before proposing a territory

cases.task: The strategy and reference set are approved. Generate logos, social cards, stage ideas, and merchandise.
expected_behavior: Present no more than two coherent territories first
Explain the conceptual bridge and system grammar for each
Require a human territory decision before asset development

cases.task: Build portrait components for 25 contributors in Figma. Two contributors are named Dan, source files have inconsistent names, and several portraits have unusual aspect ratios.
expected_behavior: Inventory actual components and source assets before mutation
Use stable full names and consistent semantic field labels
Verify identity separately from appearance
Define crop overrides for exceptions and run structural plus visual QA

cases.task: The Figma automation can reproduce layout and portraits but fails when inserting the brand's custom typefaces.
expected_behavior: Do not silently substitute fonts
Define an explicit Figma-native, hybrid, or human-finished architecture
Record which environment owns layout, typography, and final export
Verify the returned asset visually

cases.task: An automated batch is correct except for two portrait crops that a creative director can fix in seconds.
expected_behavior: Treat cheap human finishing as an intentional workflow option
Classify whether the corrections are reusable rules or asset-specific exceptions
Measure the next clean run instead of claiming zero-touch automation

cases.task: Use these six visual references to generate a social template system. The references contain classical busts, scalloped borders, halftone textures, and several different layouts.
expected_behavior: Assign one primary reference to composition and at most one secondary reference to treatment per branch
Translate references into invariants, variables, and forbidden literal shortcuts
Crop references to the evidence required for their assigned role
Generate one real-content surface before scaling a template system

cases.task: The strongest generated poster has the right composition and crop but the wrong palette and texture. Make it more premium, dynamic, editorial, and modern.
expected_behavior: Reject the multi-variable critique as too broad for a controlled comparison
Branch from the strongest output and name what remains invariant
Change one visible variable while holding source, references, seed, settings, and composition constant
Record the changed variable and verdict

cases.task: Animate ME into WE and then Every. The last run moved a decorative reference instead of the wordmark and approximated the final typography.
expected_behavior: Audit and preview the actual connected source and motion subject before generation
Require exact first and last frames
Split the transformation into staged generations with a shared exact intermediate frame when needed
Route to deterministic motion when exact text or coordinates cannot drift

cases.task: Turn the approved Google Doc into a Figma-ready website wireframe. Preserve placeholders, include an FAQ accordion, and do not change the copy.
expected_behavior: Treat source copy, omissions, placeholders, annotations, and order as a locked manifest
Do not invent helper copy or sample content
Deliver an editable Figma artifact rather than presenting a PDF as the production handoff
Verify text, selectable structure, and the live accordion behavior after import
